video_title: Bitcoin Loans Are Coming For Your Mortgage
gist: Figure CEO Michael Tannenbaum explains how integrated software, model-based underwriting and blockchain capital markets cut mortgage origination costs to about $1,000 (vs $12,000) and closing time to 9 days (vs 45), powering a capital-light 500-partner marketplace with a 'rule of 150' profile, ~60% margin guidance and expansion into investor mortgages, auto and small-business loans. Despite the title, Bitcoin-backed loans are a minor part of the discussion; the focus is HELOCs and on-chain lending infrastructure.

themes.theme: Housing affordability and the HELOC boom

insights.claim: Tannenbaum says the rate lock-in effect keeps homeowners in low-rate mortgages they won't refinance, so with home prices up they are tapping equity via HELOCs, often to consolidate debt.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Sustained HELOC demand while mortgage rates stay above locked-in rates.

insights.claim: Tannenbaum cites about $35 trillion of US home equity outstanding and says home equity is 'red hot' in the current rate environment.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Large addressable market for equity-extraction lenders.

insights.claim: Pompliano frames the midterm 'blue wave' (including Texas flipping) as driven by affordability anger, especially around home ownership.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Affordability is the dominant political issue; housing-cost policies likely.

insights.claim: Pompliano argues the K-shaped economy means wealthy commentators dismiss affordability: an $11,000 origination saving is a rounding error on a multimillion-dollar home but huge on a $100,000 loan.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Cost reduction matters most for lower-balance borrowers.

insights.claim: Figure says a mortgage on its rails costs about $1,000 to originate versus an industry average of about $12,000, which has roughly tripled in recent years.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: An order-of-magnitude cost edge makes small-balance loans profitable.
insights.quote: a mortgage done through our process is about $1,000 industry average is 12,000

insights.claim: Figure's average time to close is nine days (as fast as five), including a government-mandated 3-day wait, versus an industry average of about 45 days.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Speed is a competitive moat for partner originators.

insights.claim: Speed comes from integrating software with a built-in capital market so every loan's buyer is known, plus model-based underwriting from bank cash flows and model-based valuations instead of human underwriters and appraisers.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Removing third parties is the source of the cost advantage.

insights.claim: Putting loan attributes on blockchain cut third-party diligence costs by 80%, and on-chain tracking prevents double-pledging or double-selling loans, which Tannenbaum ties to 2008-era liar loans.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Concrete, quantified blockchain utility in credit markets.
insights.quote: We've cut 80% of the cost of third party diligence review doing that.

insights.claim: With an average loan of about $100,000, a $12,000 origination cost is 12% of the loan and untenable; Figure's lower cost opens a previously unprofitable segment of customers to partners.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Expands the addressable market to small-balance borrowers.

insights.claim: Figure settles loans with stablecoins and keeps blockchain as back-end plumbing rather than a consumer pitch, comparing it to how cloud users cared about outcomes, not the cloud.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: The winning crypto-finance model hides crypto from end users.

insights.claim: Pompliano says Figure scored about 150 on the rule of 40 (revenue growth plus EBITDA margin) last quarter; Tannenbaum says it has broken the growth-versus-margin trade-off through a franchising-like marketplace model.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Exceptional growth-plus-profitability profile for a fintech.

insights.claim: Figure's roughly 500 partners (e.g., Lowe's, regional banks, fintechs, credit unions) do the marketing and sales and fund loans off their own balance sheets, so Figure earns high-margin fees without customer-acquisition or balance-sheet costs.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Capital-light model supports high margins.

insights.claim: Figure earns an upfront marketplace fee when loans are sold (loans carry about 5-8% of value from fees and interest) plus servicing fees over the life of the loan.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Recurring servicing revenue complements transactional fees.

insights.claim: Figure does about $2 billion a month of volume, $30 billion to date, and is AAA-rated by S&P and Moody's in capital markets, against a roughly $2 trillion annual mortgage market.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Small share of a huge market leaves long runway.

insights.claim: Pompliano estimates last-quarter revenue of about $200 million (roughly $800 million annualized); Figure guides on volume and to medium-term margins of about 60%.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Key guideposts for valuing Figure.

insights.claim: Tannenbaum's biggest worry is capital markets shutting down; he positions Figure as a Fannie Mae-like liquidity provider and increasingly gets investors to commit to funding loans before origination, which only standardized on-chain assets allow.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Forward-commitment funding de-risks the marketplace in downturns.

themes.theme: Expansion: new asset classes, AI and crypto loans

insights.claim: Figure acquired the market leader in investor mortgages (about 10% share), with roughly 25% of US housing stock investor-owned, and plans to open its technology to all partners to supercharge 2027 growth.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Acquisition-plus-marketplace conversion is the 2027 growth driver.

insights.claim: Figure is extending on-chain capital markets to auto loans, small business lending (where SBA lending is capped and slow) and personal loans, using an AI 'loan adapter' that onboards closed loans in weeks instead of months.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Broadens TAM beyond mortgages.

insights.claim: A loan-officer assistant Figure built with Sierra (Bret Taylor's company) increases conversion by about 20% and is being rolled out to all 500 partners.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: AI-driven conversion gains are a near-term growth lever.

insights.claim: About 20-25% of Figure's code is written with AI (using Cursor and Grok), and AI automates loan-deed matching; Decagon is used for customer service.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: AI is lowering both engineering and loan-manufacturing costs.

insights.claim: Tannenbaum says Figure has never lost money on its crypto-backed loans because Bitcoin and Ethereum collateral can be liquidated quickly, and wants to bring that liquidity model to other asset classes like mortgages.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Liquid-collateral lending is the template for on-chain credit.
insights.quote: We've never lost money in in that product because of how quickly Bitcoin in particular or Ethereum you you can liquidate the loan.

insights.claim: Tannenbaum predicts AI agents with relentless patience will overcome borrower inertia (the top reason people didn't refinance student loans at SoFi) and naturally route consumers to low-cost providers like Figure.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Agentic finance could compress lender margins and reward low-cost rails.

insights.claim: Figure built regulatory resilience for policy 'ping-pong': licensed in all 50 states, money transmission and crypto licenses, a broker-dealer, and its yield-bearing stablecoin (transcribed as 'yields') was approved under the Biden administration.
insights.speaker: Michael Tannenbaum (CEO, Figure)
insights.so_what: Regulatory moat reduces political risk after the blue wave.
